items.heading: Strip Away the Creative Glamour
items.text: Strip away the creative glamour and a typical day looks like this: ingesting and organising raw footage, syncing audio to picture, building a rough assembly, then shaping that assembly for pacing, story, and emotional beats, before a colour pass and an audio mix turn it into something ready to publish. A large share of the job is organisation and discipline, not just creative cutting; a messy, unlabelled project file slows down every step after it.

items.heading: Tools Matter Less Than Most
items.text: Tools matter less than most beginner content suggests, but three of them show up in almost every real job posting and freelance brief, and depth in each one buys you something different.

rows: Owns the cut end to end for a project: pacing, structure, sound, basic colour, and titles, working from a brief with some creative discretion.
Three to five finished, published pieces where you made the structural and pacing calls, not just executed someone else's timeline.
Handles the hardest or highest-stakes cuts, sets the pacing and style direction for a project, and gives feedback on junior editors' work.
A track record across enough projects that a producer trusts you with an ambiguous brief and no supervision.

Branches from editing into deeper After Effects work: full motion graphics, animated brand systems, or explainer-style animation. This is a related but genuinely different skill ladder, not an automatic next step.
A reel built specifically around animated graphics and motion design, separate from your cuts-based editing reel.
